open_points.subject: personal-data boundary for direct agent service access
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class” and A07’s “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value” conflict with “An agent's own access to a service … is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel” and “its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on agents receiving personal-data content apply globally, including direct service access, or only to values returned through the kernel surface?
options: The prohibition applies only to kernel responses; direct services may return personal-data content to agents
The prohibition applies globally, so direct service access must also prevent agents receiving personal-data content
Direct access is allowed only for service data not classified as `personal_data`
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as a kernel-surface guarantee only, because the new exclusion expressly limits it to what the kernel returns.

open_points.subject: kernel listener exposure
open_points.text: “The proxy … is the only client of the kernel's listener, whose address the installation names and which the host does not expose otherwise.”
open_points.question: What makes or verifies that the configured listener is reachable only by the reverse proxy?
options: The kernel accepts only a loopback or Unix-socket listener
The kernel accepts any configured address and relies entirely on host configuration
The kernel authenticates the reverse proxy separately from ordinary owner and agent tokens
open_points.default_guess: Rely on host configuration and perform no kernel-side proxy-only verification, because the text assigns exposure to the host.

open_points.subject: TLS before the reverse proxy
open_points.text: “The proxy terminates TLS …; tokens therefore travel encrypted up to the proxy.”
open_points.question: Is TLS on the client-to-proxy path a required condition that installation or acceptance must verify, or merely an assumed host property?
options: Installation must verify or attest that the proxy accepts only TLS
Acceptance verifies the deployed proxy externally
The kernel assumes the host provides TLS and performs no check
open_points.default_guess: Treat TLS termination as an external host assumption that the kernel does not check.

open_points.subject: disposable-rig rehearsal equivalence
open_points.text: “the owner runs a second kernel installation whose services select their `disposable_rig` instances, and runs the flow there as anywhere else.”
open_points.question: What must be the same between the rehearsed flow on the second installation and the production flow, given that installations have separate records and bindings have randomly minted identities?
options: Manually recreate equivalent contracts, implementations, bindings and flow content, allowing different record identities
Transfer an exact package of records between installations
Require only behaviorally similar rehearsal, without defined artifact equivalence
open_points.default_guess: Manually recreate equivalent artifacts and accept different installation-local identities, because no transfer mechanism exists.

open_points.subject: effectful-flow rehearsal requirement
open_points.text: “Effectful flows are rehearsed on an installation of disposable rigs” but “The rehearsal is the owner's practice, not a kernel step — no kernel requires, records or checks one, and activating a flow does not depend on it.”
open_points.question: Is rehearsal a normative acceptance requirement requiring evidence outside the kernel, or only recommended owner practice with no enforceable or testable obligation?
options: It is a normative requirement verified through external acceptance evidence
Every effectful flow must be rehearsed, but compliance is accepted solely on the owner's assertion
open_points.default_guess: Treat rehearsal as recommended external practice and implement no kernel behavior for it.
